data.text/markdown:
🧠 Research Conclusion

Statistical Analysis Summary

  • Correlation Coefficient (||(r \approx 0.51||)): Indicates a moderate, positive linear relationship between rent and size. As the size of the property increases, the rent tends to increase as well.
  • P-value (||(\approx 5.81 \times 10^{-11}||)): This value is significantly lower than the standard alpha threshold of 0.05. Therefore, the result is statistically highly significant, meaning the observed correlation is extremely unlikely to have occurred by random chance.

Research Conclusion

There is a statistically significant, moderate positive correlation between property size and rent. While property size is a clear factor influencing rental pricing, the moderate strength of the correlation (||(r \approx 0.51||)) suggests that other variables—such as location, building amenities, local market demand, or property age—play a substantial role in determining rental rates. Increasing square footage does not guarantee a proportional increase in rent, indicating that size is only one of several key determinants in the housing market.
